title: H7 – Rewards II: how to pay
source: Zusammenfassung von Session 7 „Rewards and compensation part 2“ (Sayre et al., 2026; Groysberg, 2021; National Office Supplies)

blocks.text: PFP can raise performance and attract high performers, but it can also cause competition, stress, burnout and turnover (Dahl & Pierce, 2020).

The harm comes from pay uncertainty: uncertainty → insecurity → overwork and neglected recovery → stress and burnout (Sayre et al., 2026). Fix it with clear rules, smoothed variable income and more financial security.
Collective PFP is positively related to collective outcomes (Nyberg et al., 2020) but trades alignment against line of sight and risks free riding.
How to pay (Groysberg, 2021): fixed vs variable, short vs long term, cash vs equity, individual vs collective – balancing direction, fairness and workability.
Herzberg: compensation is a hygiene factor; rewards and compensation are different things.
Pay transparency ranges from confidential to full; the EU directive requires firms to explain and justify why people are paid differently.
Uncertainty mechanism (Sayre et al., 2026)
Clear, Smooth, Secure
children: Clear: KPIs and criteria in advance, frequent feedback

blocks.text: Collective PFP (Nyberg et al., 2020)
children: Alignment vs line of sight; free riding, inequity, conflicting incentives

blocks.text: Groysberg (2021)
children: Fixed vs variable · short vs long term · cash vs equity · individual vs collective

blocks.text: Herzberg's two-factor model
children: Hygiene: policy, supervision, relations, conditions, compensation
Motivators: achievement, recognition, work itself, responsibility, growth

blocks.text: Equity theory (Adams)
children: Compare own outcome/input ratio with a referent's

blocks.text: Pay transparency
children: EU directive: pay ranges before hiring, no salary-history questions, right to information, gap reporting (100+ employees), ≥ 5 % unexplained gap → joint pay assessment

sections.heading: Applying H7 to a case (National Office Supplies)

blocks.text: 1. Analyse reward practices with the course frameworks
children: What to pay for: internal consistency, external competitiveness, individual contributions
Types of rewards: financial and non-financial

blocks.text: 2. Recommend two specific changes and justify them with the course
children: e.g. written bonus criteria for all offices (clear) and an office-level team share instead of a monthly winner (smooth)
e.g. turn the discretionary London pot into a secure London allowance (secure)

blocks.text: London (Jeff): strong but volume-only link to performance, high uncertainty and discretion – “pay for performance without certainty”. Scotland (Nicola): equal split, recognition and contact – “certainty without pay for performance”.
Critical points: the sums are modest, the experiments used simple lab tasks, the case shows no direct burnout evidence – and Scotland's equal split risks free riding.
Uncertainty about what performance will be rewarded and how much an employee will earn.
How clearly an employee sees the connection between own effort, performance and reward.
Pay contingent on collective outcomes: team PRP, gainsharing, profit sharing, stock options.
Factors whose absence causes dissatisfaction / factors whose presence creates satisfaction (Herzberg).
Employees know how pay is determined / employees know the resulting pay levels and gaps.
What should employees have a right to know about pay?
Summary: two key questions on rewards – “what for” and “how to pay” (not merely “how much”); PRP is common but controversial and depends on the PM system.
